verdict.rationale: Glama's directory says every server is scanned and scored, and the product supports comparing servers. Community users confirm a TDQS quality score with letter grades. Docs also mention verified ownership via a claim token, which acts as a verification signal. Missing for 10: documented usage or popularity counts; health or liveness checks; first-party docs explaining how the score is computed or how it appears on listing pages; a documented verification badge; and reliable score re-testing, since two users report retests stalling for days because of an undocumented credit-card requirement.

support.subject: As a developer, I can compare servers using published quality signals — usage counts, health or liveness checks, scores, or verification badges

citations.quote: Search, compare, and connect to thousands of MCP servers
